idiom_name: plain objects or classes in a domain module + explicit mapper functions in the data layer
implementation_notes: JavaScript needs no framework to separate the models: the domain module exports classes (private fields, methods, frozen value objects) or plain objects plus pure transition functions, and the data layer owns the ORM models (Sequelize/Prisma/TypeORM) together with toDomain/toPersistence mapper functions. What replaces the classic Mapper is a pair of small functions per aggregate; what makes the separation necessary is that ORM instances carry dataValues, lazy getters and save() behaviour, and that JSON/spread round-trips drop prototypes - so domain objects must be reconstituted through their constructor or factory, never assembled field by field from a row. With no type system, the mapper and boundary validation are the only places where shape drift is caught.
pitfalls: Object spread or JSON.parse produce 'domain' objects without a constructor call, so invariants are never checked - reconstitute through the class/factory instead.
ORM instances leak upward: a Sequelize model handed to a service drags its dataValues, association getters and save() into business code and blocks database-free tests.
N+1 queries hide behind the mapper: mapping a list of rows one by one without include/eager loading issues a query per entity.
